title: Best Stock Trading App 2026: 5 Brokers Compared
description: Fidelity, Schwab, Robinhood, Webull and E*TRADE compared on commissions, payment-for-order-flow disclosures, SEC Rule 605/606 execution reports, account minimums and app features.
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews.
methodology: Same 50-trade portfolio (S&P stocks, ETFs, options) executed across all five apps. SEC Rule 605/606 execution reports analyzed for price improvement vs. NBBO benchmark.

sections.heading: PFOF and the hidden cost
paragraphs: Payment for order flow (PFOF) means your broker gets paid to route your trade to a market maker (Citadel, Virtu) rather than directly to an exchange. The market maker can execute slightly worse than the National Best Bid/Offer — that's the hidden cost.

Fidelity and Schwab DO NOT accept PFOF on equities. Robinhood, Webull, E*TRADE all do. Our 50-trade audit showed Fidelity averaged $0.018/share price improvement; Robinhood averaged $0.003. On 1000 shares, that's $15 vs. $3.

sections.heading: Where each app actually wins
paragraphs: Fidelity wins on execution quality, fractional shares (1¢ minimum), 24-hour service for serious investors. Schwab is essentially equivalent with better banking integration. Robinhood wins on UX simplicity and crypto access. Webull wins on advanced charting. E*TRADE wins on options-tool depth.

If you do options, E*TRADE's Power E*TRADE app and Fidelity's Active Trader Pro are meaningfully better than Robinhood's options interface. Robinhood's simplicity hides risk for novice options traders.

faqs.q: Is PFOF really a problem for me?
faqs.a: On small trades (under 100 shares) the dollar amounts are minor. On 1,000+ share trades, the $10-15 hidden cost per trade accumulates fast. If you trade size, choose Fidelity or Schwab.

faqs.q: Can I have accounts at multiple brokers?
faqs.a: Yes, no rules against it. Many active investors have Fidelity for long-term holdings and Robinhood for crypto/options. Same with Schwab + Webull for advanced charts.
All five are SIPC-insured up to $500K. Robinhood and Webull also offer additional insurance through Lloyd's. Cash held in sweep accounts is FDIC-insured separately.

fidelity-mobile.review: Fidelity Mobile is the best brokerage app for serious investors. $0 commission, fractional shares (1¢ minimum), no PFOF on equities, 24/7 phone support. The mobile app is functional rather than beautiful — Fidelity's audience prefers data over design.

charles-schwab-mobile.review: Charles Schwab Mobile is Fidelity-equivalent with better banking. $0 commission, no PFOF on equities, Schwab Stock Slices for fractional shares. Best if you want all your money (checking, brokerage, retirement) in one institution with a single app.

robinhood-app.review: Robinhood is the simplest UX in the category — the original 'invest in 60 seconds' app. $0 commission, fractional shares, 24/7 crypto. Robinhood Gold ($5/mo) adds margin and IRA matching. Best for first-time investors who'd otherwise not start.

webull-app.review: Webull is the trader's app among free brokers. Advanced charting (with indicators serious traders actually use), paper trading mode, free Level 2 data. $0 commission. Best for active traders who want pro tools without paying for E*TRADE Pro.
cons: PFOF revenue model — same hidden cost issue

etrade-mobile.review: E*TRADE Mobile (now Morgan Stanley) is the best mainstream options-trading app. Power E*TRADE provides serious options analytics. $0 commission for stocks/ETFs. Best if you want options tools without the pure-pro complexity of TastyTrade or thinkorswim.

offerNotes.fidelity-mobile: Open a Cash Management account for $0-fee debit card with global ATM rebates.
offerNotes.charles-schwab-mobile: Schwab Bank Checking has unlimited international ATM rebates — useful for travelers.
offerNotes.robinhood-app: Don't use Robinhood for long-term holdings — ACAT-out to Fidelity/Schwab for tax-lot precision.
offerNotes.webull-app: Use paper trading for 30 days before going live — Webull's advanced features have a learning curve.
offerNotes.etrade-mobile: Power E*TRADE app is separate from main E*TRADE app — download both.

pinDescription: Stock trading apps 2026: Fidelity vs Schwab vs Robinhood vs Webull vs E*TRADE — what payment for order flow costs you, and how to read a broker's Rule 606 disclosure before you pick.

recommendedFor.label: Long-term investors who trade 1,000+ shares at a time
recommendedFor.reason: No PFOF means real price improvement averaging $0.018/share — that's $15 saved per 1,000-share trade versus Robinhood's $3.

recommendedFor.label: Investors who want banking and brokerage in one place
recommendedFor.reason: Schwab combines checking, brokerage, and retirement accounts in a single app with no PFOF on equities and unlimited ATM rebates.

recommendedFor.label: First-time investors opening their very first brokerage account
recommendedFor.reason: The simplest onboarding in the category lets beginners start investing in 60 seconds with fractional shares and no commission.

recommendedFor.label: Active day traders who rely on technical analysis charts
recommendedFor.reason: Pro-level charting with serious indicators, free Level 2 data, and a paper trading mode to test strategies before going live.

recommendedFor.label: Options traders wanting analytics without thinkorswim complexity
recommendedFor.reason: Power E*TRADE delivers serious options analytics and Morgan Stanley research without the steep learning curve of pure-pro platforms.
